title: Add multiplexed fanout + adaptive cursor-shard coordinator to cut dashboard tail latency
creator: Diego Martinez
description:
Problem: Certain dashboard queries (tenant top-K, multi-metric time windows) exhibit long tail latency spikes under bursty exploration workloads. Root causes we identified in telemetry: uneven shard fanout amplification for multi-range queries, suboptimal cursor placement causing repeated re-seeks, and head-of-line blocking when a single slow shard stalls merged pagination.

Goal: Implement a lightweight multiplexed fanout layer that aggregates and multiplexes upstream query requests to reduce duplicate per-shard work, and introduce an adaptive cursor-shard coordinator that shards cursor ranges by request hotness and tenant quantile to minimize re-seeks and balance load across replicas. The solution should reduce p95/p99 query latency for dashboard explorations by at least 30% without increasing average CPU cost by more than 10%.
acceptance_criteria: p95 latency for top-K dashboard queries reduced by >=30% in canary traffic vs baseline
p99 latency reduced by >=25% and no new 99.9th percentile regression
end-to-end increase in per-query CPU/IO <=10% on average during canary
feature flag controls: multiplexed fanout and cursor-shard coordinator can be toggled independently
automated integration test that simulates bursty exploration showing stable pagination across 10k tenants
no functional regression for existing pagination semantics (cursor continuity, stable ordering)
technical_notes: Multiplexed fanout: add a thin layer in the query router which coalesces concurrent subrange queries per-shard for the same logical dashboard request window and returns a multiplexed stream to the merger. This reduces duplicate disk/kv lookups and amortizes serialization costs.

Adaptive cursor-shard coordinator: maintain a lightweight in-memory map of active cursors with per-tenant heat scores; hot cursors are sharded into smaller range buckets and pinned to different replicas to spread load. Cold cursors fall back to merged coarse-grain cursors to keep memory low.

Backpressure & hedging: implement request hedging for stalled shard RPCs with a configurable delay (default 50ms) and prefer hedged replica with freshest cache entry. Metrics must track hedged vs non-hedged success rates.
Compatibility: keep existing cursor encoding (opaque token) but include a coordinator version byte so older clients fall back to safe behavior.
KV cache interplay: multiplex layer will consult prefix-KV cache to avoid unnecessary fetches; must invalidate multiplex entries on eviction events.

Observability: new metrics - multiplex_coalesced_requests, cursor_shard_splits, hedged_rpcs, shard_queue_wait_ms, and per-tenant quantile heat score. Add tracing spans for fanout/coalesce/merge steps.
implementation_plan: Spike (2d): prototype multiplexed fanout in a branch of query-router using a local in-process coalescer; run microbenchmarks against synthetic multi-range workloads to validate savings
Design review (1d): share design doc with infra and platform teams, finalize failure modes and feature gate semantics
Implement multiplexed fanout (3d): add coalescer, integrate with existing shard RPC client, add unit tests and basic metrics
Implement cursor-shard coordinator (4d): build coordinator with heat scoring, cursor split/merge algorithms, and per-tenant pinning; include fallback path
Backpressure & hedging (2d): add hedging logic and replica preference hooks; ensure cancellation flows properly
Integration tests (2d): extend test harness to simulate 10k tenants, bursty exploration patterns, and verify cursor continuity
Canary rollout (3d): enable feature flag for 5% traffic, monitor metrics and dashboards; iterate on thresholds
Gradual ramp (7d): 5% -> 25% -> 60% -> 100% with abort-on-regression gates defined by SLOs
rollout_plan: Feature-flagged rollout. Start with internal canary (dev + staging), then 5% production traffic for telemetry baseline comparison for 48h. If criteria pass, ramp to 25% for 72h, then 60% for 48h, and full rollout. Abort conditions: p95 regression > 5% from baseline, hedged_rpcs error rate > 1%, or increased error responses for pagination endpoints. Post-rollout: run a 7-day verification window and capture performance snapshots for release notes.
risks: Cursor-splitting could increase memory footprint if many hot cursors are split; mitigation: conservative heat threshold and LRU-based demotion
Incorrect coalescing may introduce ordering anomalies if merge step mishandles duplicate ranges; mitigation: strict idempotency checks and deterministic merge logic
Hedging can amplify load if thresholds are too aggressive; mitigation: start conservative and add backpressure controls
Cross-tenant fairness: pinning hot cursors to replicas might starve other tenants on same replica; mitigation: integrate tenant-weighted scheduling and enforce replica fairness quotas
